events.title: May Fourth Movement
events.short: In 1919 the Paris Peace Conference rejected China's just demands; on 4 May Beijing students marched shouting “Secure sovereignty abroad, punish traitors at home”, and China refused to sign.
events.detail: After World War I the victorious powers, including Britain, the United States, France and Japan, held a “peace conference” in Paris from January to June 1919. China, as one of the victors, sent delegates, who put forward just demands: abolition of the powers' privileges in China, cancellation of the “Twenty-One Demands”, and the return of Germany's rights in Shandong that Japan had seized during the war. They were refused, and the conference decided to transfer Germany's rights in Shandong to Japan. On 4 May 1919, more than three thousand students from over a dozen Beijing schools gathered before Tiananmen, shouting slogans such as “Secure sovereignty abroad, punish traitors at home” and marching in demonstration, demanding punishment of the pro-Japanese officials Cao Rulin, Zhang Zongxiang and Lu Zongyu. Angry students burned Cao Rulin's residence, Zhao Jialou, and beat Zhang Zongxiang. From 5 June, Shanghai workers staged large-scale strikes in support, the movement's center shifted from Beijing to Shanghai, and the working class stepped onto the political stage. The “three strikes” (of students, merchants and workers) then spread to more than twenty provinces and over a hundred cities. Under pressure from the people, the Beiyang government was forced to release arrested students and dismiss the three pro-Japanese officials. On 28 June the Chinese delegates refused to sign the treaty, a first victory for the movement. The May Fourth Movement was a thoroughgoing anti-imperialist and anti-feudal patriotic movement and the beginning of China's new-democratic revolution. The May Fourth spirit that took shape in it, of “patriotism, progress, democracy and science”, has had lasting influence, and 4 May was later designated Chinese Youth Day.

events.title: Early Communist Groups Established
events.short: In 1920, with Comintern help, Chen Duxiu founded the first early communist group in Shanghai; groups followed in Beijing, Wuhan, Changsha and elsewhere, including overseas.
events.detail: After the May Fourth Movement, Marxism spread widely in China and gradually merged with the Chinese labor movement, and conditions for founding a Communist Party matured. In spring 1920 the Comintern sent Voitinsky and others to China. In August 1920, with Comintern help, Chen Duxiu and others founded China's first early communist group in Shanghai, with members including Li Hanjun, Li Da, Chen Wangdao and Yu Xiusong, and Chen Duxiu as secretary. The Shanghai group coordinated and promoted party-building elsewhere. In October Li Dazhao and others founded an early communist group in Beijing. Groups were then established by Dong Biwu, Chen Tanqiu and others in Wuhan, Mao Zedong, He Shuheng and others in Changsha, Wang Jinmei, Deng Enming and others in Jinan, and Tan Pingshan and others in Guangzhou; groups also formed among Chinese students and overseas Chinese in Japan and France. Once founded, the groups studied and propagated Marxism in an organized way: they published periodicals such as the monthly The Communist and Marxist works such as the complete Chinese translation of The Communist Manifesto; went into factories to organize workers, ran night schools and helped set up trade unions; and founded the Socialist Youth League, training a body of revolutionary cadres. These activities promoted the merging of Marxism with the Chinese labor movement and prepared the ground ideologically and organizationally for the formal founding of the Communist Party of China. In July 1921 delegates from the groups held the First National Congress in Shanghai, proclaiming the Party's formal founding.

events.title: Founding of the Communist Party of China
events.short: The Party's First Congress opened in Shanghai on 23 July 1921, with its last session held on a boat on South Lake in Jiaxing, Zhejiang, proclaiming the founding of the Communist Party of China.
events.detail: After the May Fourth Movement, Marxism spread widely in China, early communist groups were set up in many places, and conditions were ripe to found a unified national Communist Party. On 23 July 1921 the First National Congress of the Communist Party of China opened at 106 Wangzhi Road (now 76 Xingye Road) in the Shanghai French Concession. Thirteen delegates attended, representing more than 50 Party members nationwide: Mao Zedong, Dong Biwu, Chen Tanqiu, He Shuheng, Wang Jinmei, Deng Enming, Li Da, Li Hanjun, Zhang Guotao, Liu Renjing, Chen Gongbo, Zhou Fohai and Bao Huiseng. The Comintern representatives Maring and Nikolsky also attended. Chen Duxiu and Li Dazhao did not attend for various reasons. On the evening of 30 July the meeting place was searched by French Concession police and the congress was interrupted; its last session moved to a pleasure boat on South Lake in Jiaxing, Zhejiang. The congress adopted the Party's first program, named it the “Communist Party of China”, and set its goals as overthrowing bourgeois rule, establishing a dictatorship of the proletariat, abolishing class distinctions and realizing communism, with organizing and leading the labor movement as its central task. It elected the Central Bureau, with Chen Duxiu as secretary. The founding of the Party was an epoch-making event in Chinese history: the Chinese revolution now had a strong leading core and a completely new look. 1 July was later designated the Party's founding anniversary. The site of the First Congress in Shanghai and the Red Boat on South Lake in Jiaxing are important revolutionary memorials.

events.title: Nanchang Uprising
events.short: On 1 August 1927 Zhou Enlai, He Long, Ye Ting, Zhu De, Liu Bocheng and others led the Nanchang Uprising, firing the first shot in armed resistance to the Kuomintang reactionaries.
events.detail: After the Great Revolution failed, the Kuomintang reactionaries' policy of bloody massacre provoked fierce resistance from the Communist Party and the revolutionary masses. Learning from the defeat the importance of independently holding armed forces, the Party decided to launch armed uprisings. In July 1927 the Central Committee decided to stage an uprising in Nanchang and set up a Front Committee headed by Zhou Enlai to lead it. The participants were mainly units that the Party controlled or influenced, including the National Revolutionary Army's 20th Army, the 24th Division of the 11th Army and the Nanchang Officers' Training Corps led by Zhu De, over 20,000 men in all. In the early hours of 1 August, led by Zhou Enlai, He Long, Ye Ting, Zhu De, Liu Bocheng and others, the rebels attacked the Kuomintang troops garrisoning Nanchang; after more than four hours of fighting they wiped out over three thousand defenders and took the city. Under the Central Committee's original plan, the rebel army then left Nanchang and marched south toward Guangdong. In the Chaozhou–Shantou area of Guangdong it was besieged by Kuomintang troops and its main force was defeated; the remnants, led by Zhu De and Chen Yi, later went up Jinggangshan and joined the forces led by Mao Zedong. The Nanchang Uprising fired the first shot of armed resistance to the Kuomintang reactionaries, marking the start of the Party's independent leadership of armed struggle and of building a people's army. In 1933 the Provisional Central Government of the Chinese Soviet Republic designated 1 August as the founding anniversary of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army; it later became Army Day of the People's Liberation Army.

events.title: Four Crossings of the Chishui and Luding Bridge
events.short: After Zunyi, Mao Zedong directed the Red Army across the Chishui four times, the Jinsha and Dadu rivers and Luding Bridge, and over snow mountains and grasslands, shaking off its pursuers.
events.detail: After the Zunyi Conference the Red Army was reorganized and its fighting power rose. From late January to late March 1935 Mao Zedong directed the Central Red Army around the Sichuan–Guizhou–Yunnan border, feinting east and striking west, crossing the Chishui four times, threatening Guiyang and Kunming, drawing in and destroying enemy troops on the move and upsetting the Kuomintang's pursuit plans. In early May the Red Army skillfully crossed the Jinsha River (upper Yangtze), escaping encirclement by hundreds of thousands of enemy troops. In late May it reached Anshunchang on the Dadu River, where seventeen heroes crossed in a small boat and forced the river. With too few boats for the main force, the Red Army marched hard along the west bank, covering 120 kilometers in a day and a night to reach Luding Bridge. The bridge was formed of thirteen iron chains, its planks removed by the enemy, and twenty-two assault troops climbed along the chains under fire to the far bank and took the bridge. In June the Red Army crossed the perpetually snow-covered Jiajin Mountain and joined the Fourth Front Army at Mougong. Zhang Guotao then opposed the Central Committee's northward course, and the Central Committee led the First and Third Army Groups north. In August the Red Army entered the vast grasslands, where many soldiers gave their lives; it came out through extraordinary endurance and in September broke through the natural barrier of Lazikou. On the Long March the Red Army crossed eighteen mountain ranges, five of them perpetually snow-capped, and twenty-four rivers, achieving a miracle in human history. Mao wrote the poem “The Long March”: “The Red Army fears not the trials of the distant march; to them the thousand mountains and rivers are nothing.”

events.title: Marco Polo Bridge Incident
events.short: On 7 July 1937 Japanese troops, claiming a soldier had gone missing, attacked Wanping and the Marco Polo Bridge; Chinese defenders resisted, and the incident began China's all-out War of Resistance.
events.detail: On the evening of 7 July 1937 Japanese troops stationed at Fengtai, southwest of Beiping, held military exercises near the Marco Polo Bridge and, claiming that a soldier had “gone missing”, demanded to enter Wanping town to search, which Chinese troops sternly refused. The well-prepared Japanese then attacked Wanping and the bridge, and the Chinese defenders, the regiment of Ji Xingwen of the 37th Division of the 29th Army, resisted. This was the incident that shocked China and the world, known as the July 7th Incident or Marco Polo Bridge Incident. It marked the start of Japan's long-planned full-scale war of aggression against China and of the whole nation's resistance. The day after, the Communist Party telegraphed: “Peiping and Tianjin are in peril! North China is in peril! The Chinese nation is in peril! Only resistance by the whole nation is our way out!” On 17 July Chiang Kai-shek said at Lushan that “if war once begins, there will be no distinction between north and south, old and young; everyone will have the responsibility of defending the land and resisting, and must resolve to sacrifice everything”. In late July Japanese troops launched a general attack on Beiping and Tianjin, and Deputy Army Commander Tong Linge and Division Commander Zhao Dengyu died heroically at Nanyuan. By the end of July Beiping and Tianjin had fallen. In September the Kuomintang's Central News Agency published the Communist Party's declaration on Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, and Chiang made a statement in effect recognizing the Communist Party's legal status, marking the formal formation of the anti-Japanese national united front based on cooperation of the two parties. The nationwide resistance began.

events.title: Nanjing Massacre
events.short: After Japanese troops took Nanjing in December 1937, over six weeks they killed more than 300,000 Chinese civilians and disarmed soldiers in appalling atrocities.
events.detail: After the Battle of Shanghai, Japanese troops advanced on Nanjing in three columns. They took the city on 13 December 1937; the National Government had already announced the move of the capital to Chongqing, designated the wartime capital. After the occupation the Japanese army carried out a bloody massacre in and around the city lasting six weeks, killing Chinese civilians and disarmed soldiers by mass shooting, live burial, hacking and burning; the dead numbered over 300,000. Japanese troops also raped women on a massive scale, looted property and burned buildings. Japanese newspapers even openly reported a “killing contest” between two army second lieutenants. During the massacre more than a dozen foreigners who stayed in Nanjing, including the German John Rabe and the American Minnie Vautrin, organized the International Committee for the Nanjing Safety Zone, set up the Safety Zone and protected over 200,000 Chinese refugees. The American missionary John Magee filmed the Japanese atrocities, leaving valuable historical evidence. The Nanjing Massacre was one of the gravest crimes committed by Japan in its war of aggression against China and an appalling atrocity in the history of human civilization. After the war, the International Military Tribunal for the Far East and the Nanjing War Crimes Tribunal tried the main persons responsible, sentencing war criminals including Matsui Iwane and Tani Hisao to death. In 1985 the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders opened. In 2014 the NPC Standing Committee designated 13 December each year as the National Memorial Day for Victims of the Nanjing Massacre. In 2015 the Nanjing Massacre Archives were inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.

events.title: National Resistance: Zhang Zizhong and Zuo Quan Fall
events.short: In the War of Resistance, all ethnic groups, parties and classes fought together, and commanders such as Zhang Zizhong of the 33rd Army Group and Zuo Quan of the Eighth Route Army died heroically.
events.detail: Under the banner of the anti-Japanese national united front, people of all ethnic groups, parties, political factions and strata, along with overseas Chinese, set aside differences, united against the aggressor and fought together. In May 1940, in the Battle of Zaoyang-Yichang, Zhang Zizhong, commander of the 33rd Army Group, personally led his troops across the Xiang River (Han River), but was surrounded by Japanese forces at Nanguadian in Yicheng, Hubei. Hit by several bullets, he kept commanding until he died a martyr's death at 49. Zhang was one of the highest-ranking Allied generals killed in World War II, and Mao Zedong wrote the elegiac inscription "Loyal to the end, serving the country." In May 1942 the Japanese army launched a major "mopping-up" of the Taihang Mountains, where the Eighth Route Army headquarters was based. Zuo Quan, deputy chief of staff of the Eighth Route Army, was struck by a shell at Shiziling in Liaoxian, Shanxi, while commanding troops covering the headquarters' breakout, and was killed at only 37; he was the highest-ranking Eighth Route Army officer to die in the war. In his memory Liao County was renamed Zuoquan County. Elsewhere, Yang Jingyu of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army kept Japanese forces at bay in the ice and snow until he died fighting when out of ammunition and food; when the Japanese cut open his stomach they found only dried grass, bark and cotton wadding. Zhao Yiman endured brutal torture after her capture and never yielded. The Five Heroes of Langya Mountain of the Eighth Route Army led the enemy onto a dead end to cover the retreat of civilians and the main force, then leapt off a cliff. Ethnic minorities also took an active part in the war; the Hui Detachment led by Ma Benzhai was hailed as the "ever-victorious Hui Detachment." The unity of the whole nation in resistance was the fundamental reason for victory.

events.title: Victory in the War of Resistance Against Japan
events.short: Japan announced unconditional surrender on 15 August 1945 and signed the instrument of surrender on 2 September, ending the war of resistance in victory; Taiwan was returned to China.
events.detail: From 1944 to early 1945, news from the world anti-fascist front was a stream of victories, and Germany's defeat in Europe was assured. Germany surrendered unconditionally in May 1945. On 26 July China, the United States and Britain issued the Potsdam Proclamation urging Japan's unconditional surrender and reaffirming that the Cairo Declaration must be carried out, requiring Japan to return the Chinese territories it had stolen, including the Northeast, Taiwan and the Penghu Islands. On 6 and 9 August the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. On 8 August the Soviet Union declared war on Japan and sent troops into northeast China. Under heavy blows from the Chinese people and anti-fascist forces worldwide, the Japanese emperor announced unconditional surrender on 15 August 1945. On 2 September Japanese representatives signed the instrument of surrender aboard the US battleship Missouri in Tokyo Bay. On 9 September the surrender ceremony for the China Theater was held in Nanjing, where Okamura Yasuji, commander-in-chief of Japanese forces in China, handed the instrument of surrender to He Yingqin, commander-in-chief of the Chinese Army. On 25 October the ceremony for Taiwan was held in Taipei, and Taiwan and the Penghu Islands, occupied by Japan for fifty years, returned to China. The Chinese people's War of Resistance was the first war of national liberation in modern times in which China completely defeated a foreign invader, and the Chinese theater was the main Eastern theater of the world anti-fascist war. In fourteen years of resistance, Chinese military and civilian casualties exceeded 35 million, an enormous national sacrifice. After the victory, China became a founding member of the United Nations and one of the permanent members of the Security Council. In 2014 the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress designated 3 September as Victory Day of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japan.

events.title: Crushing the Key-Point Offensive (Shaanbei and Menglianggu)
events.short: In 1947 Kuomintang forces made key-point attacks on northern Shaanxi and Shandong; Mao Zedong led the Party Central Committee through northern Shaanxi, and the East China Field Army wiped out the 74th Division at Menglianggu.
events.detail: In March 1947, after the general offensive had been blunted, Kuomintang forces turned to key-point attacks on the Shaanbei and Shandong liberated areas. In northern Shaanxi, Hu Zongnan led over 200,000 men against Yan'an, while the Liberation Army there numbered only some 20,000. To preserve its strength, Mao Zedong decided to evacuate Yan'an voluntarily, saying: "If we keep the men and lose the land, both men and land will be kept; if we keep the land and lose the men, both men and land will be lost." Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai and Ren Bishi led the Party Central Committee organs in remaining in northern Shaanxi to direct the national war of liberation, while Liu Shaoqi, Zhu De and others formed the Central Working Committee and went to North China. Peng Dehuai and Xi Zhongxun led the Northwest Field Army in "dawdling" tactics, wearing the enemy down, and won three battles in a row at Qinghuabian, Yangmaghe and Panlong, destroying over 14,000 enemy troops and stabilizing the situation in northern Shaanxi. In Shandong, the Kuomintang massed 450,000 troops against the liberated area. In May 1947 the East China Field Army under Chen Yi and Su Yu concentrated superior forces and wiped out the entire reorganized 74th Division, over 32,000 men, in the Menglianggu area of Mengyin County, Shandong, killing its commander Zhang Lingfu. The battle crushed the Kuomintang's key-point offensive in Shandong. The people of the Yimeng mountain area gave eager support to the front, and moving stories emerged such as that of the "Red Sisters of Yimeng," who nursed the wounded with their own milk. By June 1947, after a year of fighting, the Liberation Army had destroyed 1.12 million Kuomintang troops, the key-point offensive had been crushed, and the course of the war had turned in the Liberation Army's favor. The Liberation Army then moved to a strategic offensive.

events.title: Founding of the People's Republic of China
events.short: On 1 October 1949, 300,000 soldiers and civilians gathered in Tiananmen Square for the founding ceremony, where Mao Zedong proclaimed the establishment of the Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China.
events.detail: On the afternoon of 1 October 1949 the Central People's Government Council held its first plenary meeting at Zhongnanhai, appointing Zhou Enlai premier of the Government Administration Council and foreign minister, Mao Zedong chairman of the People's Revolutionary Military Commission, and Zhu De commander-in-chief of the People's Liberation Army. At 3 p.m., 300,000 soldiers and civilians gathered in Tiananmen Square in Beijing for the grand founding ceremony. Chairman Mao Zedong solemnly proclaimed from the Tiananmen gate tower: "The Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China is established today!" and pressed the button himself to raise the first Five-Star Red Flag. Fifty-four cannons then fired a 28-gun salute, symbolizing the 28 years of struggle of the Chinese people under the Communist Party. A grand military parade followed, in which Commander-in-Chief Zhu De reviewed the naval, ground and air forces and read the Order of the Headquarters of the Chinese People's Liberation Army. After the parade the crowds marched, and the celebrations continued into the night. The founding of the People's Republic was an epoch-making event in Chinese history. It ended more than a hundred years of humiliation by invasion and enslavement, making China a truly independent country; from then on, the Chinese people stood up and became masters of their country; and it ended long division and achieved a high degree of national unity and unprecedented ethnic solidarity. After the founding, the Soviet Union and other countries successively recognized the People's Republic and established diplomatic relations with it. In December the Central People's Government decided to make 1 October the National Day each year.

events.title: Socialist Transformation Largely Completed
events.short: From 1953 China carried out socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and capitalist industry and commerce, largely completed by the end of 1956, establishing the basic socialist system.
events.detail: After the founding of New China, the country was in a period of transition from New Democracy to socialism. In 1953 the Party Central Committee formally put forward the general line for the transition period: over a fairly long time, to gradually achieve socialist industrialization and gradually carry out socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and capitalist industry and commerce, known as "one industrialization and three transformations." After land reform, peasants had land, but agriculture was still small-scale peasant farming by individual households. The state therefore guided peasants along the road of mutual aid and cooperation, from mutual-aid teams to elementary and then advanced agricultural cooperatives, gradually changing private ownership of the means of production to collective ownership. Handicrafts were also organized into cooperatives. For capitalist industry and commerce the state adopted a policy of peaceful redemption, using state-capitalist forms such as processing orders, state purchase and marketing, and joint state-private operation to turn capitalist private ownership gradually into socialist public ownership. In early 1956 a high tide of socialist transformation swept the country. In joint state-private enterprises, capitalists received a fixed interest of 5 percent a year on their shares. By the end of 1956 China had largely completed the socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and capitalist industry and commerce, the basic socialist system was preliminarily established, and China entered the primary stage of socialism. The transformations turned private ownership of the means of production into socialist public ownership, but they also suffered from problems such as excessive haste, crude work, changes made too fast and forms that were too simple and uniform.

events.title: First Atomic Bomb Test ("Two Bombs, One Satellite")
events.short: China's first atomic bomb was successfully exploded on 16 October 1964, followed by a hydrogen bomb and a satellite launch; the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" program greatly strengthened national defense.
events.detail: In the 1950s the United States and other nuclear powers repeatedly threatened China with nuclear weapons. To break the nuclear monopoly and nuclear blackmail and defend national security, in January 1955 the Party Central Committee made the strategic decision to develop atomic energy. In 1956 the state drew up the Long-Term Plan for the Development of Science and Technology, 1956–1967. A large group of scientists, represented by Qian Xuesen, Deng Jiaxian, Qian Sanqiang, Guo Yonghuai, Wang Ganchang and Zhu Guangya, devoted themselves to developing the "Two Bombs, One Satellite." In 1959 the Soviet government tore up its agreements, halted aid and withdrew its experts. To remember June 1959, when the Soviet agreement was torn up, the first atomic bomb was code-named "596." On 16 October 1964 China's first atomic bomb was successfully exploded at Lop Nur in the west, breaking the superpowers' nuclear monopoly. The Chinese government immediately declared solemnly that China would never be the first to use nuclear weapons at any time or under any circumstances. On 17 June 1967 China's first hydrogen bomb was successfully exploded; going from atomic bomb to hydrogen bomb took only two years and eight months. On 24 April 1970 China launched its first satellite, Dongfanghong 1, on a Long March 1 rocket. The success of the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" greatly strengthened China's national defense. In 1999 the state awarded the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" Meritorious Medal to 23 scientists and technical experts. Those involved formed the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" spirit of "loving the motherland and selfless dedication; self-reliance and hard struggle; close cooperation and daring to climb."

The Dongfeng-2 missile was successfully launched in June 1964 and, in October 1966, was combined with an atomic bomb to complete the "two bombs combined" test.

In 1955 the Chinese Communist Party released some US prisoners of war from the Korean War in exchange, allowing the missile expert Qian Xuesen and his family to return to the mainland.

Around the founding of the People's Republic, Deng Jiaxian and other scientists who had studied abroad returned to the mainland one after another. In 1993 the physicist Yang Chen-Ning wrote an essay comparing Deng Jiaxian to Oppenheimer, the "father of the atomic bomb."

events.title: Founding of the Second Artillery Corps and Missile Forces
events.short: China founded the Second Artillery Corps, its strategic missile force, in July 1966; it was the core of China's strategic deterrent and was renamed the PLA Rocket Force in 2015.
events.detail: In the 1950s, facing nuclear threats and blackmail from the superpowers, the Party Central Committee decided to develop missiles and nuclear weapons. In 1956 the Fifth Academy of the Ministry of National Defense was founded, with Qian Xuesen as president, and began developing missiles. In 1957 China formed its first missile training unit. In November 1960 the Dongfeng-1, China's first short-range surface-to-surface missile, copied from a foreign design, was launched successfully. In June 1964 the Dongfeng-2, a medium-short-range missile of China's own design, was launched successfully. On 1 July 1966, with the approval of the Party Central Committee and the Central Military Commission, the leading organ of China's strategic missile forces was formally established, and Zhou Enlai named it the "Second Artillery." It comprised strategic nuclear surface-to-surface missile units, conventional missile units and support units, and was the core of China's strategic deterrent. On 27 October 1966 China successfully tested a nuclear missile on its own territory, achieving the combination of the "two bombs." The Second Artillery continued to grow, fielding medium-range, long-range and intercontinental strategic missiles as well as conventional missiles. In May 1980 China successfully launched a long-range rocket into a designated area of the South Pacific, demonstrating the long-range strike capability of its strategic missiles. China has consistently pursued a defensive national defense policy and a nuclear policy of no first use. On 31 December 2015 the Second Artillery was renamed the People's Liberation Army Rocket Force, a service on a par with the army, navy and air force. At the 2019 National Day parade for the 70th anniversary, new equipment such as the Dongfeng-41 intercontinental strategic nuclear missile made a public appearance.

events.title: Tiananmen Incident and Fall of the Gang of Four
events.short: In April 1976 mourning for Zhou Enlai grew into the April Fifth Movement against the Gang of Four; in October the Gang was smashed, ending the Cultural Revolution.
events.detail: During the Cultural Revolution, Jiang Qing, Wang Hongwen, Zhang Chunqiao and Yao Wenyuan gradually joined forces and plotted to seize Party and state power; Mao Zedong called them the “Gang of Four.” On 8 January 1976 Premier Zhou Enlai died, and people across the country mourned him deeply. The Gang suppressed the mourning, which aroused intense public anger. Around the Qingming Festival, hundreds of thousands of people gathered spontaneously in Tiananmen Square in Beijing to mourn Zhou and denounce the Gang, and lines such as “I want to grieve, but hear the demons howl; I weep while wolves and jackals laugh. I shed tears to honor a hero; with brows raised, I draw my sword” were widely recited. The Gang slandered the mourning as a “counter-revolutionary incident,” suppressed it, and used the occasion to strip Deng Xiaoping of all his posts. Known as the “April Fifth Movement,” the event laid the popular foundation for the Gang’s later fall. Zhu De died on 6 July 1976; on 28 July a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck Tangshan, Hebei, killing over 240,000 people; and on 9 September Mao Zedong died. The Gang stepped up its efforts to seize supreme power. At this critical moment, the Political Bureau of the Central Committee, represented by Hua Guofeng and Ye Jianying, took decisive action on 6 October 1976, placing Wang Hongwen, Zhang Chunqiao, Jiang Qing and Yao Wenyuan under isolation and investigation. In one stroke the Gang of Four was smashed, ending the ten-year Cultural Revolution. People across the country rejoiced. Their fall ushered China into a new period of historical development. In 1978 the Central Committee decided to rehabilitate the April Fifth Movement.

events.title: Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee
events.short: In December 1978 the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee decided to shift the focus to economic construction and adopt reform and opening-up, a great historical turning point.
events.detail: After the fall of the Gang of Four, people eagerly hoped for a new path of socialist development. From November to December 1978 the Central Committee held a work conference, at whose closing Deng Xiaoping delivered the speech “Emancipate the Mind, Seek Truth from Facts and Unite as One in Looking to the Future,” which in effect became the keynote report of the Third Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee that followed. From 18 to 22 December 1978 the plenum was held in Beijing. It thoroughly repudiated the erroneous “Two Whatevers” policy, highly praised the debate on the criterion of truth, and reestablished the ideological line of emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts. It ended the erroneous slogan of “taking class struggle as the key link,” and made the great decision to shift the focus of the work of the Party and the state to economic construction and to implement reform and opening-up. It also examined and resolved a number of major historical questions and the merits and demerits of some important leaders, rehabilitating those involved in the Tiananmen Incident and others, and added Chen Yun to the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau, forming a second-generation central leadership with Deng Xiaoping at its core. The plenum was a turning point of far-reaching significance in the Party’s history since 1949, opening a new period of reform, opening-up and socialist modernization. In the four-plus decades that followed, China’s economy rose to second in the world and living standards improved greatly. In 2018 a grand meeting was held to celebrate the 40th anniversary of reform and opening-up.

events.title: 12th and 13th Party Congresses
events.short: In 1982 Deng Xiaoping called for “building socialism with Chinese characteristics”; in 1987 the 13th Party Congress set out the primary stage of socialism and the Party’s basic line.
events.detail: After the Third Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee, Deng Xiaoping led the Communist Party in making a series of major decisions that pushed reform, opening-up and socialist modernization forward. In September 1982 the 12th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing. In his opening speech Deng said: “Integrate the universal truth of Marxism with the concrete realities of China, find our own path and build socialism with Chinese characteristics: this is the basic conclusion we have drawn from long historical experience.” The Congress set the strategic goal of quadrupling the gross annual output value of industry and agriculture by the end of the 20th century. In October 1987 the 13th National Congress was held. It systematically set out the theory of the primary stage of socialism, holding that China was then in that stage. It laid down the Party’s basic line for that stage: to lead and unite the people of all ethnic groups in focusing on economic development, upholding the Four Cardinal Principles and persisting in reform and opening-up, striving to build China into a prosperous, democratic and culturally advanced modern socialist country, summed up as “one central task, two basic points.” It also put forward a “three-step” strategy for economic development: meet basic needs, reach a moderately prosperous level, and basically achieve modernization by the middle of the 21st century. The two Congresses charted the course for building socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Deng Xiaoping Theory gradually took shape; in 1997 the 15th Congress established it as the Party’s guiding ideology.

events.title: The “1992 Consensus” and the Wang–Koo Talks
events.short: In 1992 the two cross-strait bodies each stated orally that “both sides of the Taiwan Strait adhere to the one-China principle,” the “1992 Consensus”; the Wang–Koo Talks were held in 1993.
events.detail: As cross-strait exchanges grew closer, Taiwan set up the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) in 1990 to handle practical issues arising from contacts, and the mainland set up the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) the next year. In October 1992 ARATS and SEF met in Hong Kong to discuss how to state the one-China principle in their working-level talks. In November, after an exchange of letters and messages, the two bodies reached a consensus that each would state orally that “both sides of the Taiwan Strait adhere to the one-China principle,” known as the “1992 Consensus.” Its core is that the two sides belong to one China and work together toward national reunification. It is the political foundation of cross-strait relations and laid the basis for negotiations. In April 1993 ARATS president Wang Daohan and SEF chairman Koo Chen-fu met in Singapore, the first public talks between high-level cross-strait figures, in a non-governmental capacity, since 1949, known as the “Wang–Koo Talks.” They signed four agreements including the Wang–Koo Talks Joint Agreement. The talks marked an important historic step in cross-strait relations. Later, after Taiwan’s leader put forward separatist ideas such as the “two-state theory,” talks between the two bodies were for a time suspended. After 2008 the two bodies resumed talks on the basis of the 1992 Consensus and signed more than twenty agreements, including the Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement. In 2015 the leaders of the two sides met in Singapore. Upholding the 1992 Consensus and opposing “Taiwan independence” is the key to maintaining peace and stability across the Strait and promoting its peaceful development.

events.title: Hong Kong’s Return to China
events.short: On 1 July 1997 China resumed the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region was established, ending over 150 years of British colonial rule.
events.detail: After the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration, the Chinese government actively prepared for Hong Kong’s return. In 1990 the National People’s Congress adopted the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, setting out in law the policies of “one country, two systems,” “Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong” and a high degree of autonomy. In 1996 the Selection Committee for the first government of the Hong Kong SAR chose Tung Chee-hwa as its first Chief Executive. From late on 30 June to the early hours of 1 July 1997, the Chinese and British governments held a grand handover ceremony in the new wing of the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. At midnight on 1 July the flag of the People’s Republic of China and the flag of the Hong Kong SAR rose slowly. President Jiang Zemin solemnly declared that the government of the People’s Republic of China had resumed the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong and that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region was formally established. The return washed away a century of national humiliation, ended more than 150 years of British colonial rule and marked a great victory for the “one country, two systems” concept. After the return, Hong Kong kept its capitalist system and way of life unchanged for fifty years and continued as a free port and an international financial, trade and shipping center. The central government firmly supports the SAR government in governing according to law. In 2020 the NPC Standing Committee passed the Law of the Hong Kong SAR on Safeguarding National Security, which it said safeguards Hong Kong’s prosperity and stability. Macao also returned to China on 20 December 1999. Hong Kong’s return was an important milestone on the road to the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

events.title: 17th Party Congress and Scientific Outlook
events.short: In 2007 the 17th Party Congress wrote the Scientific Outlook on Development into the Party constitution, stressing development first, putting people first, and comprehensive, sustainable growth.
events.detail: In the 21st century China’s economy grew rapidly but also faced uneven development, mounting resource and environmental pressure, and widening urban–rural and regional gaps. In 2003 the Third Plenary Session of the 16th Central Committee proposed “putting people first and establishing a comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable approach to development that promotes the all-round development of the economy, society and people,” which became the Scientific Outlook on Development. In October 2007 the 17th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing. Hu Jintao delivered a report titled “Hold High the Great Banner of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics and Strive for New Victories in Building a Moderately Prosperous Society in All Respects.” It stated that the Outlook’s first priority is development, its core is putting people first, its basic requirement is comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development, and its fundamental method is overall consideration. The Congress wrote it into the Party constitution and set tasks such as building a harmonious socialist society and an ecological civilization. It also first put forward the concept of the “system of theories of socialism with Chinese characteristics.” Under the Outlook the state took major steps: in 2006 it abolished the agricultural tax entirely, ending the “imperial grain tax” of over two thousand years; it advanced the building of a new socialist countryside; and it introduced free compulsory education in both urban and rural areas. In 2008 China met the Wenchuan earthquake and the international financial crisis and hosted the Beijing Olympics. In 2010 its GDP passed Japan’s, making it the world’s second-largest economy. The Outlook was written into the Constitution in 2018.

events.title: 19th Party Congress and the New Era
events.short: In 2017 the 19th Party Congress declared that socialism with Chinese characteristics had entered a new era and made Xi Jinping Thought the Party’s guiding ideology.
events.detail: In October 2017 the 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing. Its theme was: “Remain true to our original aspiration and keep our mission firmly in mind, hold high the great banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and strive to secure a decisive victory in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects.” The Congress made the major political judgment that socialism with Chinese characteristics had entered a new era, and noted that the principal contradiction in Chinese society had become the one between the people’s ever-growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. It established Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the guiding ideology the Party must uphold over the long term and wrote it into the Party constitution. It set a strategy in two stages from 2020 to the middle of this century: first, from 2020 to 2035, on the basis of a moderately prosperous society in all respects, to strive another fifteen years to basically realize socialist modernization; second, from 2035 to the middle of the century, to strive another fifteen years to build China into a prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful modern socialist country. In March 2018 the first session of the 13th National People’s Congress passed a constitutional amendment writing Xi Jinping Thought into the Constitution and establishing the National Supervisory Commission. The 19th Congress was a very important meeting held in the decisive stage of completing a moderately prosperous society, and it drew a grand blueprint for China’s development in the new era.
